tagline: where the intrusion goes next, ranked by evidence
model: LightGBM multiclass softprob over prefix-presence features
trained_on: sightings_v2 development set (original train + val splits)

evaluation.protocol: 5-fold StratifiedGroupKFold over the development set, grouped by sequence, stratified by length (DEC-18); metrics are sequence-balanced

paired_reference.note: Markov-2 minus LightGBM; LightGBM is ahead and the CI excludes zero

masking.reason: DEC-17: first-occurrence deduplication makes an already observed technique an impossible target

known_negative_results: Mined pattern features add nothing to the ranking (-0.0059); DEC-19
Tactic abstraction does not improve ranking (+0.0013, not replicated); DEC-20
Graph/Node2Vec, tactic and interaction features add +0.0012, CI straddles zero; DEC-21
Fixed-weight ensembling with Markov-2 gains +0.0005; DEC-19
caveats: Predictions rank the next technique in *reported* order, which is not established to be execution order (DEC-05: ordering is non-random at p=0.005, but non-random is not chronological).
Several next techniques are usually plausible: a reused two-technique context is followed by 6.02 distinct techniques on average. Treat the ranked list as a shortlist, not a verdict.
Top-1 accuracy is 0.369; top-5 is 0.756. Read the top five, not the top one.

Techniques already present in the prefix are excluded, because first-occurrence deduplication (DEC-03) makes them impossible targets. This is a property of the training data, not of real attacker behaviour.
Trained on 2,178 incident sequences from the CTID sightings data. Not validated on any live enterprise environment.

The raw model is over-confident; probabilities are temperature-scaled on out-of-fold predictions before display. Ranking is what the evaluation measured, so prefer rank and the observed transition counts over the probability when judging a candidate.
At least two observed techniques are required for the learned model. A single technique falls back to the first-order transition model, because every training prefix has length 2 or more.
